quotes.text: That process feels normal because it's familiar, but familiar and effective are not the same thing. A ticket is not support, a ticket is evidence that support arrived late.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the help desk ticket as a symptom of late support.

quotes.text: A chatbot waits for you to type a prompt, but an Invisible Employee watches for conditions to change. It starts from context instead of starting from a conversation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a crisp line between chatbots and autonomous support agents.

quotes.text: Because the blast radius of a support agent depends entirely on its permissions, designing those permissions is a core part of designing support.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Links agent permissions directly to support design and risk.

quotes.text: If your team saves 10 minutes on execution but burns 8 minutes cleaning up the mess, you didn't actually automate support.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the hidden rework cost of poor automation tangible.

quotes.text: The agent just becomes another layer of paint on a crumbling wall. It might answer a question faster, but it can't fix a support model that was built around delay.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns against dropping agents on top of broken processes.

chapters.title: The new ROI of invisible support
What this means for the support team
How to start with one support flow

takeaways: A ticket is evidence that support arrived late; autonomous agents in Microsoft 365 can use signals from Entra, Intune, Defender and Teams to fix friction before users ask.
Govern support agents like employees, with their own identity, a named owner, least-privilege permissions, human approval for high-impact actions and full logging.
Measure value through autonomous resolution rate, mean time to resolution, cost per resolution and regained productivity, and start with one high-friction flow.
hook: Help desk tickets only measure pain after employees have already lost time and context. This episode shows IT and support leaders how autonomous agents inside Microsoft 365 can detect and fix friction before a ticket exists, and how to govern, measure and roll out this invisible support layer safely.
